q: What is the carbon footprint of newsprint per tonne?
title: Newsprint CO2 per tonne
short: Newsprint from recycled fibre needs de-inking and pulping electricity plus steam for drying; newsprint from mechanical pulp uses a great deal of refiner electricity. Add electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh and boiler fuel, then divide by tonnes of reels.

ul: Electricity for pulping, refining and the paper machine.
Waste paper or wood bought in, as Scope 3.

p: Newsprint is a publisher's largest Scope 3 purchase. Ask the mill for its per tonne figure and fibre source.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
